Within these limits, the unrestricted model achieves modest average score gains over IID. Log-loss evidence is consistent across the reported familywise procedures for QQQ, sensitive to the procedure for IWM, and not significant for SPY after adjustment; most of the gain comes from 2015--2018 and the sign reverses in 2023--2025. The defensible claim is conditional and asset-specific rather than a stable forecasting edge, and no reversible advantage is detected under any procedure. For SPY and QQQ, most score improvement concerns middle-versus-outer probabilities, whereas the fixed allocation is locally more responsive to the conditional upper-versus-lower probability.

The economic result is arithmetic rather than a verdict on the models. A round trip costs about five basis points per session at the primary rate while the better forecast adds 0.02 to 0.07 basis points per day, so acting on these probabilities costs roughly two orders of magnitude more than the probability difference it exploits. That is why every model loses capital under this rule. It also reframes the question from whether the rule is profitable to whether a score gain is of an appropriate order of magnitude for the decision at all.

What generalises is the protocol rather than the tickers: decompose the score along the rule's arguments, adjust across contrasts and check stability across segments before calling an advantage real, and price the action before claiming economic value. Applying the same protocol to other assets will produce other conditional answers; treating one asset's result as the general one is precisely the inference this design cannot support.
new:
Within these limits, the unrestricted model achieves modest average score gains over IID. Log-loss evidence is consistent across the reported familywise procedures for QQQ, sensitive to the procedure for IWM, and not significant for SPY after adjustment. The advantage is strongest in 2015--2018 and reverses for SPY and QQQ in 2023--2025. All primary reversible-minus-unrestricted log-loss intervals contain zero; the exploratory fixed-cutpoint and early-period IWM exclusions favor the unrestricted model. No forecast advantage from detailed balance is demonstrated, and non-rejection does not establish equivalence.

The economic conclusion is specific to the decision rule. Daily liquidation makes maintaining near-half exposure costly even with uninformative probabilities. Total costs of about five basis points per day coexist with unrestricted-minus-IID net improvements of 0.02--0.07 basis points per day, but this scale comparison must not be read as the incremental cost of choosing the unrestricted forecast: mean cost differences between the two models are below 0.005 basis points per day. Absolute losses reflect realized gross returns, the baseline cost and compounding. They do not establish that a turnover-aware alternative would fail.

The contribution is the integrated diagnostic template: connect an available score factorization to the decision rule's sensitivity, assess multiplicity and time stability, and separate baseline exposure from incremental return and cost. The exact log-loss factorization provides that connection in this application. Transfer to another score, rule or holding period requires its own mathematical and empirical assessment.

\section*{Data and Code Availability Statement}
The accompanying replication supplement contains analysis code, synthetic tests, protocol documentation and source/data SHA-256 fingerprints. Its README documents environment setup, release verification and replay using locally supplied Date, Open and Close data. Third-party raw prices and row-level price-derived outputs are excluded. The archived data file is not distributed, although identifying fingerprints for it are published in the code package; a new download will not match those hashes byte for byte. The supplied replication record reports a reconstruction of the daily panel from a fresh retrieval of the same vendor series using the supplied code: row counts and date ranges match the archived fingerprint exactly, and the final-period log loss is reproduced to six decimals for SPY and IWM and to within $3\times10^{-6}$ for QQQ, without identifying which records account for that difference. The realized open-to-close returns that the models classify are invariant to a same-session adjustment factor, which can explain differing price-file hashes without differing intraday returns. Exact equality of model outputs still depends on whether any return ratios or labels changed. Appendix~B documents the reconstruction and the independent estimator. The release candidate has no permanent public repository or DOI at the time of this revision. The manuscript source package also provides the aggregate inputs and arithmetic used for the additional descriptive table. Online Appendix B distinguishes the original verification evidence from these arithmetic additions.
